hypothesis_statement.content: The Hall response is predominantly intrinsic and Berry-curvature-driven after thin-film symmetry lowering.

direct integration with silicon remains an outstanding challenge.

problem_motivation.content: Overcoming the MnTe-on-silicon integration challenge is motivated not just by materials growth, but because it is necessary for translating the physics of altermagnetism into practical, technologically relevant device architectures.

causal_claim.content: Symmetry breaking in MnTe thin films—specifically the loss/lifting of bulk symmetry constraints involving z-directed translation/inversion such as τC6z or τS6z due to the film geometry—generates finite Berry curvature and thereby enables a finite anomalous Hall conductivity/hysteretic Hall response, unlike bulk insulating MnTe with vanishing AHC.
evidence_spans: finite Berry curvature generated by symmetry breaking in the thin-film geometry.
A finite AHC emerges only when the relevant symmetry constraints are lifted [9, 10].

Being an insulator with a well-defined gap at the Fermi energy, the bulk altermagnetic MnTe demon-strates vanishing anomalous Hall conductivity and therefore epitaxially grown MnTe films are promising to induce AHC.
However, for the case of MnTe films, as these symmetries vanish, the spin quantization along z axis can give finite AHC at the Fermi level
The emergence of a finite, hysteretic Hall response in a compensated antiferromagnet highlights the critical role of symmetry breaking in enabling Berry-curvature-driven transport

In the films, as the growth direction is z, the periodicity along the z direction is killed at the surface. As a result, all symmetries that involve inversion and/or translation with respect to the z axis are absent.

hypothesis_statement.content: The observed Hall response in MnTe thin films is hypothesized to be predominantly intrinsic and driven by nonzero Berry curvature generated when thin-film geometry lowers/breaks the bulk symmetry, thereby producing a finite anomalous Hall conductivity.
evidence_spans: providing transport evidence consistent with finite Berry curvature generated by symmetry breaking in the thin-film geometry.

In thin films, the C6zt001/2 symme-try, which connects the two oppositely spin-polarized sublattices in bulk MnTe, is broken both at the surface and at the film–substrate interface. Consequently, the mag-netic point group symmetry of bulk MnTe is modified, intrinsically giving rise to a finite anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC).

The resultant band structure exhibits a non-zero Berry curvature giving rise to finite AHC as illustrated in Fig. 4(c). To investigate into this hypothesis we perform magnetoresistance and Hall resistance measurements

The combined observation of an anomalous Hall effect without a corresponding bulk net magnetization, correlated hysteresis in the longitudinal and transverse channels, weak scaling between σxy and σxx, and a finite calculated AHC following thin-film symmetry lowering supports a predominantly intrinsic Berry-curvature contribution to the observed Hall response.
